# Signal Harbor

> Signal Harbor provides managed AI search visibility, marketing execution, connected analytics, and discovery attribution for middle market and enterprise companies, delivered through a client portal. It finds where AI platforms leave a company out, describe it inaccurately, or favor a competitor on the questions buyers ask, turns the gaps that matter into campaigns and content, and shows the work, approvals, publication status, and results in one place.

This file summarizes Signal Harbor's public offer, client portal, and measurement methods.

## Who it is for

- Marketing teams at middle market and enterprise companies that want to be found, understood, and considered during buyer discovery, comparison, and evaluation in AI search
- Agencies working with several client companies, through agency partnerships

## What Signal Harbor does

The program runs as one six step loop:

1. Find: test the questions buyers ask AI platforms and show where the company is left out, described inaccurately, or passed over for a competitor, with the recorded answers and cited sources as evidence
2. Prioritize: tie each gap to a product, an audience, and an initiative, so the work starts with what matters to the business rather than every gap at once
3. Prepare: Signal Harbor prepares the pages and content the campaign calls for, written from supported company facts and ready for review
4. Review: the client team confirms facts, comments, requests changes, and approves a specific version
5. Publish: approved work goes to whoever publishes it (the client team, its agency, or as agreed for the engagement), and the portal records the published URL and date. An approved page is not counted as published.
6. Measure and improve: compare matched retests with the baseline after publication, combine visibility changes with search discovery, traffic, and tracked conversions, and use evidence-based impact estimates to improve the next campaign. Recorded outcomes and estimates keep separate labels, sources, windows, and assumptions.

## The client portal

Client work and results are delivered through the client portal.

- Home: next actions and what needs the client team's review
- Insights: the questions tested, the recorded answers, competitors named, and cited sources
- Campaign: the plan, prepared content, review, and approval
- Results: publication records, AI visibility, organic query and page performance from Search Console, and traffic sources, landing pages, and tracked conversions from Google Analytics 4. Each measure retains its source and dates.

## The offer structure

- The introductory call is free.
- Booking the call includes a complimentary AI Visibility Snapshot and live portal demo: see how AI describes and recommends the company, then explore the managed program. Client work is delivered in the portal.
- Company pilot: a 90 day minimum commitment within a six month full pilot. After the first 90 days, the client chooses whether to stop or continue at the same monthly rate. Current rates and full commercial terms are published only on the [pricing page](https://signalharborai.com/pricing/).
- The company-pilot price is the founding partner rate. Future program pricing will reflect a broader platform and delivery scope. The same monthly rate applies throughout the six month full pilot.
- Agency partnerships: contact for pricing. Agency pricing depends on the number of client companies, custom portal requirements and their costs, and the scope of the engagement.
- Included company-pilot delivery: one campaign plan per month, five content templates per week, and the client portal for evidence, prepared work, review, approvals, publication records, and results.
- Company-pilot audit coverage: eight AI answer platforms, comprising ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Meta AI.
- Included intelligence and connections: Signal Harbor AI for context-aware content work; Agent Connections for approved company context and campaign workflows; Google Analytics 4; Google Search Console; and AI search, SEO discovery, and attribution. These are part of the offer companies sign up for.

## Key definitions

- AI visibility: how often, how accurately, and how favorably AI platforms present a company when buyers ask them to compare options or recommend providers
- Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): the practice of improving how generative AI systems describe and recommend a company in the answers they produce
- Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): the practice of structuring content so systems that return direct answers can find, interpret, and reuse it accurately
- Mentioned versus recommended: an answer can name a company without recommending it, so the two are recorded separately, along with answers where the company is not mentioned at all
- Matched retest: the same buyer questions asked of the same AI services after the work is published, so later answers are compared with the baseline on equal terms

## Boundaries

Signal Harbor measures observable AI visibility signals across selected platforms and buyer questions. Results can vary by model, location, account state, prompt wording, source availability, and time. Signal Harbor does not control AI systems and does not guarantee placement, ranking, mentions, recommendations, leads, or sales outcomes.
